Fixed before the first run (Helios's spec): Stage A PASS = exactly |n| zero modes of D_GW at every (N, n) with N in 4..20, n in 0..6, n < N. Notation: N = 2L+1 is the matrix size of the base fuzzy sphere (Venus: brane count / resolution), n = number of strings = monopole
charge. The charge-n sector is the AIN block L' = L^(a) = L - n/2 of A_i = L_i x 1 + 1 x T_i with T = n/2 (AIN eqs. 3.40-3.43),
i.e. fermions are 2-spinor-valued (2L'+1) x (2L+1) matrices, A_i acting from the left as spin L', L_i from the right as spin L.
Operators as written in AIN: a = 1/(L+1/2) (2.18); Gamma^R = a(sigma.L^R - 1/2) (2.16); H = a(sigma.A + 1/2) (2.19);
Gamma^ = H/sqrt(H^2) (2.17), = (sigma.L' + 1/2)/(L' + 1/2) on the block (3.30); D_GW = -a^-1 Gamma^R (1 - Gamma^R Gamma^) (2.23);
index = (1/2) Tr(Gamma^R + Gamma^) (2.28), = 2(L - L') on the block (3.37) [standard: AIN].

## Round-sphere targets [standard; sympy]

AIN block index 2(L - L') with L' = L - n/2: n [standard: AIN (3.37)].

## Stage B [prediction] - lowest three nonzero levels against the round sphere (graded on n/N)

delta_k = |lambda_k^fuzzy / lambda_k^round - 1|, lambda_k^round = sqrt(k(k+n)) (sympy target above), k = 1..3; degeneracy checked against n + 2k per sign. Rules (fixed before the run; Venus's additions agreed by Helios): the scan covers n = 0..N-1 at each N; n* is found by linear interpolation in n between the neighbouring integers n0, n0+1 that bracket delta_1 = 0.1 (first crossing), and x* = n*/N; the bracketing pair is printed; delta_1 at n = 0 is printed as the finite-N floor.
Fold-in (Venus): the last two columns use a prefactor built from both spins, the geometric mean of the base-spin and charge-sector normalisations, a_gm = sqrt(a a_s) with a = 1/(L+1/2) and a_s = 1/(L'+1/2): D_gm = -a_gm^-1 Gamma^R (1 - Gamma^R Gamma^). Gamma^R and Gamma^ are unchanged (Gamma^R keeps a, so (Gamma^R)^2 = 1); AIN's (A.1) allows any invertible O(a) prefactor. The AIN-as-written columns, x* and the grade rule are unchanged.

The drift is [identity: prefactor convention] (pattern first seen in a prototype before the graded run; verified numerically, not proved analytically): every positive level of D_GW in the block is lambda_k = sqrt(k(k+n) N/(N-n)), k = 1..N-n. Max relative deviation over all printed levels = 1.0e-14; level ratios lambda_k/lambda_1 equal the round ratios to max |rel. difference| = 6.0e-15. So the drift is a uniform rescaling by sqrt(N/(N-n)) = sqrt((2L+1)/(2L'+1)), the same for every k, and delta_1 = 1/sqrt(1 - n/N) - 1 reaches 0.1 at x = 1 - 1/(1+0.1)^2 = 0.173554. The per-N spread in x* comes only from the linear interpolation on the integer-n grid.

Reading [computed]: in the charge +n block the largest charge that exists is n = N - 1 (L' = 0). There D_GW has the N-1 zero modes and one other level, at the cutoff value 2/a = N, with degeneracy N+1: no smooth levels are left. For n >= N the block L - n/2 does not exist. In the literal isospin construction the lowest block of A_i is then |L - T| = T - L, whose index is 2L - 2(T - L) = 2(N-1) - n, i.e. the index turns back down (N-2 at n = N, N-3 at n = N+1) instead of growing. The opposite orientation (charge -n) exists for every n.

## Notes

- Bonus [standard]: the Stage B targets lambda^2 = k(k+|n|), degeneracy |n|+2k, are also the angular levels of a charged spin-1/2 particle on the
  S^2 of a magnetically charged black-hole horizon (near-horizon AdS_2 x S^2), where the flux through S^2 plays the role of n (Wu-Yang monopole harmonics).
- Venus: N = brane count / resolution, n = number of strings; the n = 3 zero modes form j = 1 and rotate with d^1(beta) (checked above).
- Scope [standard]: the zero-mode count is topological (the index; it cannot change under small deformations), while the number and
  position of the excited levels depend on the cutoff and on the prefactor convention (rungs = N - n; drift = prefactor choice).
- Helios's reading [standard; Orion verifying]: an N-state fuzzy sphere is the lowest Landau level of a charge-(N-1) monopole
  (F. D. M. Haldane, Phys. Rev. Lett. 51 (1983) 605). Linking this to Akitti's bubble, where each string spends one unit of a fixed
  flux budget, is [assumed].
